profile.reading: Alembic Computer Services, Inc. is a small Arizona business software consultancy, not a data center. Operating under the name Alembic Computer Services from an office near South 48th Street in Tempe, the firm provides custom programming, custom reporting, and integration consulting built around QuickBooks and Acctivate inventory management software, along with point of sale connectors for retail systems including Blaze, Treez, and Meadow. That is accounting and business software consulting work, the kind of service a small IT shop performs for other companies computers, not the leasing of power, cooling, and rack space that defines a commercial data center or colocation facility. The coordinates recorded for this listing sit in a mixed office and light industrial stretch of Tempe near Phoenix Sky Harbor, an area that hosts many small technology and services firms of exactly this kind. Nothing in the company's own published material describes owning or operating server halls, uninterruptible power systems, or leased colocation space for outside tenants. This entry is best understood as a mapping mismatch, a small consulting office labeled with a data center tag it does not fit, rather than as evidence of an actual data center at this address.
profile.research_note: Confirmed via WebFetch that acsi-az.com (redirects to alembiccomputerservices.com) describes Alembic Computer Services Inc as a QuickBooks/Acctivate accounting software integration and consulting firm, phone 602-454-9222, not a data center or IT infrastructure provider. Nominatim reverse geocode places the OSM node at 2125 S 48th St, Tempe AZ, an office/light industrial area. Confident mistag of a small business software consultancy. Note: alembic.com is an unrelated SaaS company (causal AI analytics) with no connection to this listing.

reading.body:
This entry does not describe a data center. Alembic Computer Services is a software consulting firm providing accounting and business system integration services near Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport, not an operator of colocation infrastructure. The firm's own published materials describe custom programming, QuickBooks integration, and point of sale consulting work. No specifications for power capacity, cooling systems, or leased rack space are published.

The mapping of this address as a data center facility appears to be a classification error. The physical location sits in a mixed office and light industrial area of Tempe typical of small technology service firms, not in a zone or facility designed for server operations. Confirmatory research found no published evidence that this business owns or operates server halls, uninterruptible power systems, or colocation space for outside tenants.

This listing should be disregarded in any assessment of Arizona's data center capacity. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities in this database, but only four publish power figures totaling 512 MW. This entry contributes neither confirmed megawatts nor meaningful infrastructure to that total.
